cycles.title: The Older Inhabited World
cycles.eyebrow: Kingdoms, commercial roads and metropolitan inheritances occupy an already old world.
cycles.description: The older world is already inhabited and contested. Living practitioners sustain local communities while councils, courts and armies make competing claims on public protectors. Territorial campaigns encounter lands with purposes of their own; compacts limit what crowns can possess. Schools and traveling professions coexist with commercial roads through older political worlds. Later metropolitan trades openly handle some workings while households keep other knowledge privately. Nell and Bash eventually inhabit a low-magic society after earlier technological and magical ages.
cycles.sequenceNote: This proposed orbit brings together overlapping regional cultures before a later metropolitan reach and Nell's trough. A village, a professional school and a military road can depend on one another without representing successive stages of progress. Windows locate broad reaches rather than convert local years into orbital duration.

eras.title: The tended watersheds
eras.description: Crops, water, health and household routines depend on living practitioners whose work has accumulated over years.
context: A maintained barrier, seasonal plant work and many small village favors support ordinary settlement life; residents still need tools, labor and practical knowledge.
A private researcher's experiment and visiting surveyors expose different failures: coercion in one case, and a mistaken model of circulating favors in the other.
eras.sequenceNote: These established communities overlap the towns, schools and territorial campaigns. Lanternscrape's visiting specialists connect rural dependence to a wider professional world; a village is not simply an earlier stage of a city.

eras.title: The occupied marches
eras.description: Expanding powers encounter lands and lives whose existing purposes obstruct military possession.
context: Three successor crowns pursue a former custodian through changed uplands. Elsewhere, a punitive grain seizure drives a deserter's disastrous intervention in a village harvest.
Mixed refuges, beast runs, protected approaches and a dragon's nest obstruct military or extractive ambitions. Local inhabitants retain purposes that the invading power may misread.
eras.sequenceNote: These territorial conflicts have different rulers, causes and outcomes. A century of successor rule and twenty years outside a trapped sunset are separate local histories. Neither evacuation nor negotiated withdrawal establishes a common peace.

eras.title: The people called heroes
eras.description: Public protection can be a chosen feat, a civic office, or a duty that other people try to impose.
context: Nemea's rules recognize a champion while excluding her witness from the deed. A court-appointed hero wears armor that diverts danger onto nearby protectors.
An armored rooster protects a road across both armies' wars. A cloister's private experiment produces a remarkable rescue without making its practitioner a public employee.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed neighboring cultures distribute heroic power and credit differently. They overlap working communities and professional schools before Nell's later low-magic home. Their practices are not established ancestors of the later public sky or hero agencies.

eras.title: The households and working towns
eras.description: Paid labor, practical care and private ambitions connect wealthy households with working shops and shared public rooms.
context: Royal guarantees and household commands meet the limits of actual work. A roof still needs sound materials and willing hands; wages and wrongful dismissals remain obligations after a magical crisis ends.

Living gracework and protective perfume operate beside ordinary tools, accounts and music. The Bellweather household must preserve consent in unenchanted ink, while a hereditary club confronts survivors its official roll has erased.

Long-lived carers raise children whose lives move faster than their own. Elsewhere, friends meet over paid food and music in a town where furniture already accommodates tails. Work, pleasure and family life continue beyond the ambitions of a court.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed neighboring cultures with distinct households, institutions and populations. Their livelihoods can coexist in an older magic-active world; no common charter, species ancestry or sequence of their personal events is established.

eras.title: The limits of a crown
eras.description: Crowns depend on agreements with people and jurisdictions they cannot simply absorb.
context: Dragon allies retain their own obligations; a military service bargain assigns wages and responsibilities beyond the palace.
Sanctuary kingdoms protect dispersed heirs, a baroness preserves her jurisdiction, and an imperial bride invokes an outside tribunal.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed neighboring political cultures understand allegiance as a negotiated relationship. Their treaties differ; a successful bargain in one kingdom does not reform the emperor in another.

eras.title: The schools and working professions
eras.description: Qualification, teaching and working appointments shape who can practice a capacity and which communities can receive that work.
context: Kethra's qualification and later teaching form a direct local history; other practitioners confront assessment, sponsorship and access to training.

Lacebridge's municipal fencing yard trains patrol workers and teachers. Fiora's accepted head-instructor post takes her upriver to East Weir; the local bout and supper leave that professional move intact.
Road rotations and a seasonal shelter circuit take skilled care beyond the school. A technical annex must recognize living collaborators and provide access to its instruction.
eras.sequenceNote: Kethra's pair stays together. The other institutions form a proposed professional horizon with distinct rules and sources of power. Lacebridge's ordinary training supplies no common magical system or institutional ancestry. The Cinder Annex is placed by its educational context while its physical coordinate remains unresolved.

eras.title: The roads through older worlds
eras.description: Caravans, mines and traveling livelihoods cross landscapes whose structures and political histories are already old.
context: Cooling contracts, freight credit, mine work and dockside processing keep trade moving; ordinary travelers depend on paid lodging and work in the next town.
Delvers find traces of earlier visitors. An isolated wizard recalls imperial commerce, but his first guest in centuries cannot tell him which of those distant institutions still exist.
eras.sequenceNote: These working corridors overlap the chartered towns and professions. The wizard's isolation does not prove a general collapse. The Night Harvest's underlying category and old-versus-new position remain unresolved; this is its proposed operating context.

eras.title: The crossings people work for a living
eras.description: Doorway repair, witnessed passage and everyday transport encounter extraordinary routes as practical work.
context: A doorway apprentice can issue a certificate; an exit witness and clinic handle a dangerous crossing economy.
Courier and municipal workers meet older road customs that their stored directions cannot explain.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed metropolitan neighbors share occupations and practical contact with crossings. Knowledge is uneven even among specialists; no common portal network is established.

eras.title: The inheritances kept at home
eras.description: Families and partners carry powers, objects and encounters whose personal history matters more than any public classification.
context: A boxed pendant, a mother's wig, a hospitality custom and a family watch reach new holders with unfinished obligations.
Private body changes, an unexpected double and encounters across unequal clocks require trust that relatives and partners cannot assume.
eras.sequenceNote: These households can overlap the practiced metropolitan trades. Keeping an identity or an object private does not by itself show that magic is fading; Nell's later home supplies the actual low-magic landmark.

eras.title: Nell and Bash’s low-magic home
eras.description: One familiar modern society treats magic largely as a story after earlier ages of technology and active power.
context: Philadelphia and Cambridge continue their ordinary routines around two brief departures.
Nell and Bash bring 617 shared days in Ravel back into separate home clocks.
eras.sequenceNote: This home era precedes later divine rises and the Glass Sea. Ravel is another pre-extinction era of the same world, with its order relative to those eras unresolved.

cycles.title: The Returning Sovereignties
cycles.eyebrow: Gods, human governments and a public magical sky follow different fortunes.
cycles.description: After Nell's older modernity, living gods and extraordinary capacities again shape later societies. Northbridge's concealed international aid occupies an earlier reach than schools and city skies where powers have become ordinary public knowledge. Elsewhere, long-lived governments transfer responsibility, harbor rites sustain passage, and royal families confront the claims made on their lives. Forests grow through older kingdoms while other inhabited places adapt their inherited works. Solstice's vanished circles belong to one loss within this plural world. The later Glass Sea still has living powers, technical crews and a political inheritance to repair.
cycles.sequenceNote: Nell's home precedes later divine rises. The hidden-to-public transition is an editorial reconstruction, with no known disclosure event or institutional descent. The Bay and Glass Sea remain ordered landmarks; neither ends all magical societies before the Ascendancy.

eras.title: The hidden circles of Northbridge
eras.description: Young practitioners extend concealed help beyond Northbridge, whose everyday culture treats magic as fiction or an effect.
context: The power cut prevents anyone witnessing a transformation. Names beside blurred costume footage leave a promotional-stunt explanation plausible to classmates.
Three afternoons later, one contact card begins months of connections across oceans through ordinary travel and communication.
eras.sequenceNote: Attendance leads directly to Help. This reconstruction places their concealed network substantially before the ordinary public sky; the emergence of public recognition between them remains an open history.

eras.title: The guarantees people live under
eras.description: Water, grain and everyday safety depend on long-lived institutions whose promises shape what people can decide for themselves.
context: Kharost's rulers divert public water toward private sleep; an inquiry and elected councils lead to cooling works on a separate watershed.
The Sleepless Majesty's conflicting grain judgments give way to a ninety-day bargain between farmers and importers, revised after the first measured shortfall.
Sablewake's nine living readers enforce a witnessed future at a cost to their own memories. Three centuries of guaranteed outcomes have left ordinary rescue services without reserves.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed regional contemporaries have different institutions and outcomes. An invented ancestral cult ends, an actual collective god abdicates, and a binding prophecy is irreversibly broken. None of these local changes ends magic throughout the world.

eras.title: The harbors of living powers
eras.description: Shipwrights, crews, harbor officers and priests work where living powers affect tides, launches and safe passage.
context: Brackwater's two congregations maintain a shared route through rival divine jurisdictions. The priests complete its renewal while keeping their separate allegiances.

Mallowbreak's misrule rite briefly gives an ageless shipwright authority over harbor water. Imprecise commands move danger toward neighboring coves; crews, runners and an old relief gate make her return to mortality survivable.
The truce remains in force and the shipwright remains answerable to her court. Neither story ends with ordinary work or public obligations disappearing.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed maritime contemporaries with distinct ports, rites and living powers. Their relative order, trade between them and any shared ritual ancestry remain unknown. A working truce is not a failed government, and one temporary godhood is not the founding or fall of a pantheon.

eras.title: The families inside the succession
eras.description: Royal succession, coerced marriage and return from exile place public claims inside private relationships.
context: A terminally injured king's children confront a voluntary transfer of office. Their forecast reports the act without compelling it; another kingdom recognizes a minor through evidence, witnesses and a bounded regency.
A century of bridal processions supplies living bodies to a southern heat network. One bride's return exposes the cost while leaving the fire's casualties and the next political response unknown.
Clarimond retakes her capital after seventeen years, but Belda has built a household of her own. A restored crown gives the queen no claim to recover her caregiver's intervening life.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed neighbors share dynastic pressures without a common succession law, family or war. Accepting an office, interrupting a coercive treaty and returning to an occupied capital have different consequences; the stories do not establish one regional collapse or restoration.

eras.title: The schools and the inhabited public sky
eras.description: Powers are publicly taught, classified and employed, while families and cities dispute the demands that come with them.
context: Ordinary and magical education coexist; specialized teaching, family foci, delivery flight and weather work shape an inhabited public culture.
Brackenport rejects the civic costs of hero organizations. A divine household keeps its identity private while continuing relationships with worshippers.
eras.sequenceNote: This later public reach is proposed after Northbridge's concealed network. No school or hero agency is its proven descendant. Not About That precedes the Bay; Brackenport's institutions and Cusco's family have no established part in the disappearance of Solstice's circles.

eras.title: The forests and occupied foundations
eras.description: Living forests, old refuges and settlements occupy ground whose history exceeds their current maps and routines.
context: Reused halls, orchards and abandoned roads gradually become woodland. Newly joined roots change a living forest's reach beyond its old boundary stones.
Young refugees bring knowledge that an ancient mortuary keeper lacks. Their changing signals, her carried sensations and altered flues together turn the temple into a refuge.
A thousand years of settlement records cannot predict a moving hand. Local knowledge of water, routes and households keeps residents alive while they relocate onto the forearm.
eras.sequenceNote: These local histories can overlap functioning states elsewhere. Woodland growth need not follow one destruction, the northern threat has no established link to the royal dragons, and the moving colossus proves neither divine resurrection nor a common cause for other catastrophes.

eras.title: The Bay and its long aftermath
eras.description: The last magical girl defends an evacuated bay after her circles have already vanished; later institutions inherit the event unevenly.
context: Solstice’s coronation precedes the battle by centuries.
Damaged recovery records and a museum centuries later produce different errors about who survived and what happened.
eras.sequenceNote: Battle, detention aftermath and museum stay in order within one local trajectory. The museum’s pre-extinction placement is editorial; its witness is Solstice, not the prisoner.

eras.title: The Glass Sea and the working border cities
eras.description: Living powers and technical crews sustain cities over the physical remains of earlier political decisions.
context: The Glass Sea preserves four centuries of centralized solar dependence after the Day of Glass.
Vantress combines living powers, ceramic structures and pressure signals in a different civic network.
eras.sequenceNote: The Glass Sea follows Nell and the Bay. Its second dawn is a specific recovery; Vantress supplies a compatible municipal context without sharing that catastrophe or solar root.

cycles.title: The Extinction and the Human Works
cycles.eyebrow: A vigorous magical world ends; later people build and lose wonders of their own.
cycles.description: The Ascendancy grows from armistice councils after route wars and furnace invasions, seeking to bind every root while magical cities and societies remain active. All Accounts Due ends the old magical capacity while leaving whatever ordinary matter can sustain. After an unmeasured interval, engineering cultures keep cities, workshops and maritime communities working. Orison's permanent grounding is one later technical loss; other inhabited places continue.
cycles.sequenceNote: Extinction lies inside this proposed orbit. Its remaining reaches belong to the perfectly magicless Long Dark; matter, populations and ordinary knowledge can persist. The schematic gap after extinction represents an unmeasured history rather than an immediate reconstruction generation.

eras.title: The Ascendancy and the last accounting
eras.description: A postwar institution turns a vigorous, connected magical world toward universal compulsion and an irreversible response.
context: The Array is already 302 years old; Faris’s thirty-one years of travel encounter active cities, palaces and distinct living systems.
All six terminal conditions end the old roots and their restoration paths.
eras.sequenceNote: This is the universal extinction boundary, not the aftermath of the Bay or the Day of Glass. The later reaches of this orbit retain no old magical capacity.

eras.title: The working machine cities
eras.description: Paid workshops, inspectors and civic records sustain working infrastructure; possessing the knowledge to replace a part does not ensure the work gets done.
context: Coal, steam, quarry work and speaking-wire signals organize civic labor. At North Rise, the director deferred maintenance before the disaster and later commissions a permanent rebuild.
Hearthchain's guild record describes a completed replacement where a temporary splice actually remains. Repair knowledge survives, while false attribution hides unfinished work.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed neighboring industrial traditions within the Long Dark. Their dates and any relationship between the workshops remain unresolved; neither is identified as a first generation after extinction.

eras.title: The inhabited machine coasts
eras.description: Mobile cities depend on continuing skill, collective navigation and decisions made for whole populations.
context: A sailing city's newly operating forecast service requires one authoritative route song. Practical navigation becomes bound to an unproved account of an earlier loss.
Orison's nuclear lift system fails irreversibly; surviving residents must leave by sea. Its inhabited neighbors still possess working vessels.
eras.sequenceNote: The shared context is maintained mobile settlement, not common machinery or an established fleet. Orison remembers human building after magic's death. Its permanent grounding is a local loss, distinct from the sailing city's new forecast capacity.

eras.title: The arsenal beyond remembered knowledge
eras.description: A later agrarian community encounters technical capacity whose purpose it can no longer identify.
context: The launch facility survives physically while its operating knowledge is inaccessible.
The finders leave its controls unused and mark the hazardous route for others.
eras.sequenceNote: Placing this knowledge loss after a represented nuclear height is a historical proposal. The facility is not Orison, and neither its builders’ fate nor an earlier launch is established.

cycles.title: The Human Refoundings
cycles.eyebrow: Ordinary modernity, reconstructed antiquity and another technological height.
cycles.description: Ordinary modern life occupies one island of the Long Dark. Later technical societies make bodily alteration and artificial persons part of daily life, but disagree over who controls those lives. City records govern access to housing and work, while shared repair keeps different communities connected. Merneith builds an empire through utilities and costly political bargains. Elsewhere, workers and former military bodies contest the reach of command. Freight and skilled watch crews sustain inhabited orbits, where machinery must also account for existing nonhuman life.
cycles.sequenceNote: These proposed histories overlap rather than form a ladder from a kind society to an oppressive one. Modernity and the Queen's reconstruction share one orbital interval; the ten-thousand-year antiquity and sixty-year rise remain local spans. Advanced capacity and unequal access coexist.

eras.title: The familiar civic world
eras.description: Festivals, arts venues, cafes, schools and clinics sustain ordinary lives. Elsewhere in this proposed modern horizon, criminal households have compromised the police.
context: Volunteer radios and physical street closures coordinate a festival; staffing, transport deadlines and working equipment constrain an arts showcase. People make time for family and courtship alongside those shared tasks.

Cafe staff learn the limits of knowing a customer. A clinic records two people's choices in one medical chart. Familiar institutions must respond to what people actually say, rather than treat routine observations as permission.

Elspeth's criminal house depends on crews and compromised police. Forged orders turn trusted procedures against her, and stopping one raid leaves the wider city and its unsettled obligations in place. Ruth's life belongs provisionally to this modern horizon; her afterlife follows its own local services.
eras.sequenceNote: Our ordinary modern time belongs to the Long Dark. These stories form a proposed civic horizon with no established common city, year or government. Ruth is placed by her originating life; the afterlife station remains outside the material clock. Local Seattle names do not import literal Seattle history.

eras.title: The bodies people live in
eras.description: Modified and artificial bodies belong to ordinary households, clinics and repair economies, with personal needs that their engineering cannot decide.
context: Repairs, replacement parts and home experiments coexist with affection, money and choices about help.
Routine seedglass revisions make bodily continuity a family question even where changing one's face is commonplace.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed neighboring consumer and clinical cultures. They share practical access to bodily technology, with distinct costs and devices; they can coexist with the more coercive institutions elsewhere in this reach.

eras.title: The lives a city will recognize
eras.description: Cities and commercial institutions make safety, housing, movement and even memory depend on an authorized record.
context: An arena's return status and a tower's lease records can contradict living bodies; official recognition has immediate physical consequences.
Surveillance, an android's managed identity and neural debt expose the people and older foundations left outside the public account.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed urban neighbors share a dependence on institutional records, with different laws and technologies. Their failures occur inside functioning cities rather than proving a general technical collapse.

eras.title: The cities that must work together
eras.description: Residents and practitioners keep different capacities useful by sharing space, testing assumptions and maintaining the connections between them.
context: A repair festival discovers that an attractive invention still has to fit the people around it.
Eleven simultaneous districts survive through connected hydraulic capacities; their different architecture remains inhabited.
eras.sequenceNote: These cities provide a civic counterpoint to coercive recording systems in the same proposed technical reach. Shared repair is an alternative practice, not their proven successor government.

eras.title: The New Egyptian Empire
eras.description: Merneith's linked water, energy and weather systems grow into an empire whose shared protections make both membership and departure consequential.
context: Adults reconstructed from ancient DNA choose new lives without recovering pharaonic memories. Merneith turns an imposed museum identity into a political project.

Engineers, councils, shared courts and military protection sustain the expanding network. A coast that votes to leave waits nineteen months beyond its agreed departure while a separate shield lattice is built.
After sixty years, four people in five live within the empire. Reconstructed relatives retain lives and ambitions that their public royal roles cannot settle.
eras.sequenceNote: The ten-thousand-year antiquity and sixty-year imperial rise are local spans. Their proposed position does not date an ancient civilization against our ordinary modern island. Neighboring technical histories are not established provinces, successors or products of Merneith's empire.

eras.title: The reach of military command
eras.description: Military systems reach into civilian work, homes and embodied lives, while courts, technicians and fugitives establish different limits on that control.
context: One government's armed platform becomes leverage in a confrontation over detained maintenance workers and six hostages. Disarmament requires verifiable physical breaks and a court record.
Anvek already has voluntary control after technicians severed her remote receiver; renewed war threatens the civilian life she helped build.
Loxan escapes a Directorate that still pursues her. A ruined foundry conceals an active archive and recovery system, preserving a local institution's power inside apparently discarded infrastructure.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed neighboring histories share military uses of technical capacity. A shared government, war or legal settlement is not established. They overlap civilian body cultures and orbital work without establishing a common campaign or a single transition from captivity to freedom.

eras.title: The orbital settlements at work
eras.description: Freight crews and long-serving watch teams sustain inhabited orbital settlements through paid labor, maintenance and bounded technical decisions.
context: A tug carries refinery membranes under delivery and lease obligations. One pilot's restored neural baseline leaves lost cargo, bodily injuries and everyone else's memories in the continuing world.

For thirty years, a staffed Jovian watch has kept a living electroplasma organism below inhabited orbit. The crisis ends with all twelve pilots safe and ten working emitters, leaving no spare capacity.
eras.sequenceNote: The precise relationship between these proposed working orbital societies is unresolved. Freight contracts and a long containment watch establish different ongoing institutions. A neural baseline and a containment correlator serve different purposes; neither establishes a common military program. The watch continues after its emergency, while the ancient sunshade in the later reconstruction has an unknown construction history.

cycles.title: The Divided World and the Joined Sky
cycles.eyebrow: Road cultures and working orbits diverge; the oldest fast roads close before new magic begins.
cycles.description: Deep history has made knowledge uneven. A village moralizes bodies whose freight adaptations a caravan can partly explain; a closed pass and obsolete orbital accounts hide technically capable neighbors. Other crews maintain old structures or help a wounded vessel. The First People's destruction of the stellar lattice is a different, explicit rupture that makes its connected worlds depend on slower aid. Much later, reciprocal contact begins genuinely new magic over an already inhabited world.
cycles.sequenceNote: Ignorance in one community can coexist with knowledge elsewhere. These stories do not require one common collapse. The root burn and reawakening remain distinct events; the injured vessel has no established place before or after the burn.

eras.title: The inhabited road and water worlds
eras.description: Road communities, occupied underground spaces and contested watersheds sustain lives among uneven inheritances.
context: A civic engine survives in a salvage economy; freight adaptations persist in a population after their original methods become disputed.
Ordinary organism behavior, route knowledge, rifles and obsolete sensors support different communities.
eras.sequenceNote: These societies need not share one collapse or ancestor. Some technical loss is explicit, while other apparent ruins are inhabited places misread by outsiders.

eras.title: The neighbors history hides
eras.description: Inherited political stories and obsolete maps prevent living populations from recognizing their contemporaries.
context: A five-century closed pass conceals an orc city only two ridges away; its transport and ordinary pleasures undo the human account of a monstrous enemy.
An orbital abandonment story and old human descent maps overlook living ground communities with knowledge and purposes of their own.
eras.sequenceNote: Territorial and orbital separations make a proposed historical family. Each story establishes simultaneous living neighbors; their laws, stations, peoples and causes of isolation remain distinct.

eras.title: The skies that are still inhabited
eras.description: Pastoral communities, ordinary organisms and operating spacecraft share skies whose older structures acquire new uses.
context: An ancient sunshade shelters nests above working surface grids.
A wounded vessel and three independently answering satellites need a settlement's bell practices for a bounded local rescue.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed contemporaries within an inhabited sky. The vessel's damaged route is its own crisis; its relation to humanity's stellar lattice and the root burn is unknown.

eras.title: The burning of the stellar roads
eras.description: The First People destroy an inherited fast network to deny it to an occupier, leaving living worlds to continue without its connections.
context: A modest human home conceals functioning ancient records, root controls and coordinated listeners.
After the burn, travel takes months or years; a relief craft faces a thirty-six-day journey against forty days of remaining breathable reserves.
eras.sequenceNote: The network loss and slower relief are established within The First People itself. Other spacecraft need not use that network, and advanced civilizations continue after the burn.

eras.title: The first answer across the joined sky
eras.description: Two living answers across an external boundary begin a new material working in an already inhabited world.
context: Ordinary light carries the extinct world’s final image through ages of perfect zero without carrying a mind or magical seed.
The first bilateral link changes both participants’ worlds; other living pairs attempt their own replies.
eras.sequenceNote: This is the reawakening boundary. Earlier scenes in the same story belong to extinction and the Long Dark; the first link restores none of the six old systems.

cycles.title: The New Inhabited World
cycles.eyebrow: New magic enters many kinds of society, and local failures leave the wider world alive.
cycles.description: Mature societies after reawakening have made different arrangements for extraordinary lives. Some towns inherit obligations to local powers; some families encounter neighbors their ordinary institutions cannot explain. Other households receive practical care, while public cities recognize varied bodies and maintain professional hero services. A community that changes at eighteen has its own population history. These cultures overlap rather than take turns discovering the same thing. The Salt Crucible later destroys one proposed region while millions elsewhere continue living.
cycles.sequenceNote: An unmeasured interval separates these mature cultures from the first link. Private knowledge, clinical recognition and public professions can coexist; they are not compulsory stages of one global development. The Crucible's new-era position remains proposed and does not found the later societies.

eras.title: The working settlements and water kingdoms
eras.description: Settled communities and mobile polities negotiate the land, routes and water that support their livelihoods.
context: Sheepfolds, halls, mills, irrigation and ordinary craft continue around distinct living workings.
An orchard kingdom and a mobile cloud city occupy different positions in the same water system.
eras.sequenceNote: The cloud and land societies are simultaneous within their story. The Players Above is placed by its material town; the external players’ coordinates remain open.

eras.title: The obligations a household inherits
eras.description: Long-lived neighbors and inherited companions carry obligations into modern family life, where help, debt and ownership remain different claims.
context: Evadne releases the promises that kept her young and confined; the descendants were never magically bound. Her return to the town is voluntary.
For forty-six years, local gods divert work to postpone Valka's claim on their old debts. Their interventions consume capacity needed elsewhere and do not make her immortal.
An owner who inherited Mizzle delays a business decision while relying on the cat's compelled advice. Mizzle depends on that owner's everyday care.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed regional neighbors have long local histories, but the obligations run in different directions. Descendants do not inherit Evadne’s magical bonds; Valka retains her own claim; Mizzle’s new owner has responsibilities toward a dependent companion. No common contract system is established.

eras.title: The extraordinary lives people do not know
eras.description: Ordinary modern expectations meet hidden kin, private faculties and encounters for which the people involved lack a ready public explanation.
context: A mother fears medical misclassification; two animal rescues open relationships with kin groups that have their own customs and knowledge.
An infernal student enters a human college without appropriate medical coverage; travelers face an unexplained road event without a known institution to consult.
eras.sequenceNote: These are proposed overlapping modern communities with uneven knowledge. A hidden identity, disbelief in a faculty and an unexplained journey are different predicaments; none establishes universal ignorance of magic.

eras.title: The lives people learn to accommodate
eras.description: Households, clinicians and ordinary services learn enough about particular conditions to help people live with them.
context: A witch already knows the limits of her six erratic sneeze effects. Her friend learns to follow her decisions while an ordinary nurse advises on the fever.
An engineer builds practical accommodation for a monthly curse; a sleep-triggered displacement acquires household and property routines.
A traveler's bounded journeys and bodily costs receive clinical attention even while the faculty remains only partly understood.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed neighbors share case-specific care rather than a common power or profession. Their practical knowledge can coexist with hidden communities and public heroes elsewhere.

eras.title: The open cities and hero professions
eras.description: Cities recognize varied bodies and organize extraordinary civic service through medicine, patrols, evidence and public reputation.
context: Everyday assumptions about wings can still misidentify a person in a society familiar with several bodily origins.
Professional heroes depend on care facilities, operational records and utility systems, while families and reputations can distort accountability.
eras.sequenceNote: The three hero stories form a strong proposed professional context; the winged household supplies a compatible everyday public culture. Their coexistence is a placement proposal, with no shared agency or biological origin established.

eras.title: The community that changes at eighteen
eras.description: One community expects a bodily change at the birth minute of its members' eighteenth year.
context: Families prepare for an uncertain form, and school records anticipate correction after the change.
Friends' earlier changes provide social knowledge even though each person's outcome is different.
eras.sequenceNote: This is a distinct population custom within the proposed modern reach. It can coexist with other cultures, but it does not supply the origin of their heroes, wings, kin groups or hereditary birth marks.

eras.title: The Salt Crucible and the surviving countryside
eras.description: A premature release of worldfire destroys one region while the wider inhabited world survives.
context: An earlier rural household and ordinary travel precede the pair’s journey to the Crucible.
A valley and the western basin edge burn; surviving fields, roofs and millions of ordinary lives remain beyond them.
eras.sequenceNote: The final prose supplies the local extent of the catastrophe. Its placement after reawakening is an editorial proposal; no shared fire root, following collapse or origin of later societies is asserted.

cycles.title: The Later Refoundings
cycles.eyebrow: Working craft, long memories and advanced excavations share a later inhabited world.
cycles.description: Later cultures have built professions, family expectations and public systems around new capacities. Care must answer to the people who receive it; a hereditary-faculty society can mistake an unwanted norm for a welcome gift. Cities put living workings to use and confront the cost of controlling them. Elsewhere, excavators and a village arriving from millions of years earlier challenge the stories institutions tell about their beginnings.
cycles.sequenceNote: This is a proposed later reach with independent institutional histories. The Salt Crucible does not found these societies. Kettlebridge’s arrival shares an archaeological horizon with the coastal expedition without being declared the latest event or identifying their peoples, sites or tools.

eras.title: The care that long lives need
eras.description: Practitioners and volunteers meet lives whose memories, regeneration and bodily occupation exceed ordinary expectations.
context: A thirteen-year host search and a very old client's memory work require negotiated access to another person's body or mind.
A practitioner's experience of regenerator care exposes the limitations beneath an isolated sanctuary's claim to godhood.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed professional neighbors share learned care and its limits. Their mechanisms and personal histories differ; neither a long life nor an old sanctuary establishes the age of the others.

eras.title: The families of the birth marks
eras.description: A population expects faculties to arrive with birth marks, tying bodily identity to family knowledge, skilled work and access to intervention.
context: A family's dye work offers a place for an expected faculty; apparent absence brings stigma and a plan for a purchased graft.
The discovery of innate capacity can cost a person the practical intervention they wanted, even while relatives celebrate.
eras.sequenceNote: This hereditary-faculty culture is distinct from the community that changes at eighteen. Their comparison concerns expectations and choice; no common population or developmental mechanism is established.

eras.title: The cities of living craft
eras.description: Living capacities enter buildings, machinery, collections and public communication, where usefulness can become coercion.
context: An inhabited hall's restoration uncovers forced colony labor; an estate collection exceeds its keepers' ability to handle its contents safely.
Spellwrights and a bounded death god confront a municipal engine, while a broadcast terror scheme turns one faculty into power over a city.
eras.sequenceNote: These proposed industrial neighbors use distinct workings and have different institutions. Their technical equipment supplies a setting, while control, maintenance and responsibility explain their closer social context.

eras.title: The excavated shores and returning village
eras.description: Archaeological institutions confront physical landscapes that do not support their simple stories of royal origins.
context: A coastal expedition finds repeated communal repairs and possible deliberate retreat beneath a drowned-king tradition.
A mechanized excavation receives an intact village on the bedrock from which it vanished millions of years earlier.
eras.sequenceNote: Their shared late horizon is proposed, not a common institution or measured ordering. Kettlebridge’s departure and crossing mechanism remain unresolved; the upward water remains unclassified.

where-the-white-elk-went.note: More than three thousand autumns turn royal halls into fields, orchards and woods around one enduring witness. Its present is an inhabited palimpsest with a specific long local history.

the-last-flames.note: A long-lived keeper’s mortuary practice outlasts kingdoms she can still place. She adapts its apparatus to shelter living refugees after an elder’s death. The structures’ age and the northern catastrophe’s wider reach remain unknown.

the-villages-only-mage.note: A mountain village's mill, cistern and road depend on many accumulated living favors. Visiting certified surveyors connect that rural network to a wider professional culture; the village is not simply an earlier stage than the city.

the-ninety-year-barrier.note: A village's mills, craft work and safety depend on ninety years of a living witch's maintenance. It belongs with established watershed services, not an age before civic organization.

every-flower-she-knew.note: Eleven seasons of professional plant work connect healer, millwright and channel crews. Seasonal water logistics and trained observation place this settlement within a working rural service economy.

blood-types-of-immortality.note: Nine years of blood research take place beside mill work, winter travel and ordinary healing. The failed coercive experiment belongs to this rural technical culture; it does not establish successful immortality.

tea-for-the-first-guest.note: A roughly two-thousand-year-old tower recalls imperial leaf duties, grain fleets and horse relays while its present visitor repairs account books in a printing, coach and paid-lodging economy. The present belongs with commercial roads; the older political world is an internal historical span.

the-unfinished-sunset.note: Arveth refuses a grain seizure, then traps her own village while trying to divert the pursuing patrol. Twenty outside years and remembered repetitions of forty-three minutes expose the cost of her choice inside a collective agricultural working.

the-lions-last-constellation.note: Nemea's council requires a witness for a seven-light deed but excludes that witness from heroic participation. A failing spring makes protection urgent; Myrine and Kletho survive by departing from the authorized heroic account. This is one civic arrangement for public power, not a generic origin of magical girls.

never-a-mascot.note: Seven years of repairs let an army armorer misread an independent road protector as her side's mascot. The final rescue exposes that mistake. The bird's maker, training and original mission remain unknown; its dawn-bound growth is one capacity, not an army-wide capability.

when-the-eagle-bowed.note: A century after the Eagle Queen's execution, three successor crowns enforce incompatible warrants over a changed upland world. Yavren recovers her own previous life as a custodian, not a hereditary sovereign. The living colony remembers her revenge plan; she refuses it as well as the successors' claims.

the-gentlest-terror.note: Dragon watch, rescue and nesting rights already form an old service compact. A succession crisis tests mature institutions; the king's death is recent, while the founding obligation is much older.

strength-of-ten.note: An established old-magical history of lock tolls, grain depots and military roads. Sigrun's command is capped at twenty days; the compact assigns one-third of lock tolls to wages, injured households, roads and displaced villages for seven years.

the-bride-who-came-back.note: A century of annual bridal processions conceals the use of living brides in Cyrak's furnace, bathhouse and kiln network. Marzena returns twenty-three days after leaving Iskal; this is the interval of her absence, not the duration of the return crisis. The fire's toll, any southern retaliation and a durable replacement for the treaty remain unknown.

the-vacant-throne.note: Fifteen years of vacancy after a border war end in witnessed accession. The demon queen’s signet once administered granaries, marriages and troop roads. Political evidence and ongoing civic work fit the later old governments without a magical succession rule.

mother-of-monsters.note: A powder-using army mistakes a mixed refuge for Halwen's commanded force. Her curse produces painful warnings; refugees and beasts make independent choices. Old culverts, different body sizes and engineering knowledge determine escape routes when the assault breaks the structure.

the-kingdom-of-later.note: A rented cobbler's shop relies on a royal roof guarantee while rent and taxes remain due. Withdrawing the postponed claim gives up reimbursement; a limited repair still needs paid materials, a slater's knowledge and a ropemaker's voluntary work. The living grace protects refusals without supplying those resources.

the-shape-of-mercy.note: A landed household conceals Adrian's severance gift from him for ten years after his childhood intervention against his father. The succession crisis makes informed choice and ordinary witnessed records part of his stewardship. Tenants, damaged orchards and injured relatives remain after the magical coercion ends.

the-sister-behind-her-smile.note: Palace seamstresses, paid gracework and acoustic craft support a wealthy household. After six days of self-suppression, Odrienne cuts her anchor as the musicians disrupt the seventh-dawn cadence that would bind it. That morning she orders a review of dismissals from the previous two years.

a-note-of-spite.note: Protective perfume, music and household work support a consumer enchantment economy. Clorinda has rehearsed for her birthday beyond a thirty-year friendship's familiar roles. A defense against hexes cannot make Lavinia listen; the friend must choose to leave the song to its singer.

the-second-wearing.note: A sentient pendant survives thirty-one boxed years, several moves and family performances before entering a modern household. Wearable craft, inherited objects and ordinary work give it close contextual neighbors in this older modernity.

the-last-thing-i-could-fix.note: A court-appointed hero refuses armor designed to divert danger onto protectors. Hadrik redesigns the local device around chosen assistance, while neglected reservoir works still require ordinary craft and a crew. Its place here concerns the organization of heroic duty, not merely the smith's occupation.

where-it-hurts.note: Hiring fairs, expedition lists, souvenirs and winter lodging sustain professional adventurers. A living blade's emotional cost breaks a four-year partnership inside that commercial network.

the-seventh-night.note: A contracted delver's seven-day bodily crisis unfolds amid inns, hired travel and printed scandal. Its commercial expedition culture closely fits Where It Hurts; no shared expedition or curse is established.

clerics-infernal-ex.note: The House of Common Shelter's twenty-year circuit allows no posting beyond one season, bringing travelers care while constraining Emet's chosen life. It never forbade his relationship. Misused, bearer-powered hinge leaves threaten both the sanctuary and a working kiln court; the far side's physical coordinate remains unresolved.

fourth-house.note: Municipal assessors, guilds, insurance and permits regulate a clay worker's craft. After ten years of Gifted practice ends, Pelmara's different adult-developed capacity receives a ten-day limited license under the provisional description Cultivated. One case does not establish a universally adopted fourth category or a source shared with other stories.

voice-of-silence.note: Four years of research and an examination rescue change Kethra's standing within a callwright college. Its living geometry and hand language form the established first half of the Kethra pair.

a-lock-on-the-inside.note: Kethra is now archmage during a seven-day apprentice trial. This follows Voice of Silence in the same teaching institution; the interval between the stories remains unspecified.

the-weight-of-falling-up-rune-shoes.note: A collegium teaches practical flight through roof surveys while brooms, winged horses and rune shoes coexist. That institutional training belongs to the circulation of technical skills, not a single universal flight technology.

the-healers-measure.note: Fees, sponsorship, service terms and a twenty-seven-month capstone lead into road rotations and recurring training. Formal education feeds an itinerant public-health profession.

the-thousandth-fall.note: A season of playful, repeated self-mending practice establishes a stronger bodily baseline and culminates in a pilgrim-bridge rescue. Rasden acts by choice alongside Palla; the feat establishes neither a licensing examination nor a repeatable public service available to everyone.

the-friends-i-built.note: At the Cinder Annex, Irix's living magic shapes embermoss collaborators in brass frames. Their agency and the school's access failures determine recognition and qualification. They are living organisms, not ordinary machines generating magic; the annex's material-world location remains unresolved.

the-door-knows-home.note: Locksmith certification, estate law, appraisers and electrically served streets support a public doorway trade. Thousands of a mother's uses have made a specific dwelling recognizable; familiarity is not transferable property ownership.

an-ordinary-education.note: Delsie's laboratory origin makes her visibly unusual without making her magical. Public schools and ordinary recreation already distinguish capacities and eligibility, placing this story with Brightward and family-taught flight in a mature public culture.

not-about-that.note: Delivery work, municipal weather, roof schooling and family practice make public flight ordinary city life. Its supplied reading position is before the Bay; no shared city or direct lineage to Solstice is established.

the-small-moon-rose-first.note: Nell and Bash return to Philadelphia and Cambridge after 617 shared days in Ravel, only seconds after their separate departures. Their low-magic home precedes later divine rises and the Glass Sea. Ravel is another pre-extinction era of this same physical world, with no established order relative to their home.

a-knock-in-someone-elses-sleep.note: A quarry becomes holiday cottages while the same living mineral contact reaches two childhoods separated by sixty years. Roads, coach travel and locally concealed experience place the present within a modernity with older material layers.

a-crown-of-quiet-hours.note: A 218-year order sustains real public works through twelve dragons and forty-seven royal masks. Its fabricated ancestral cult confers no godhood. After a water diversion disables fire protection, an inquiry leads to elected councils and separate public cooling works; the intended two-century sleep is not an elapsed interval.

the-peace-they-could-sleep-through.note: Two centuries of roads, grain and collective divine adjudication leave farmers and importers appealing upward for incompatible guarantees. Their ninety-day grain bargain begins a revisable practice; the dragons surrender royal and religious authority. Godhood ends while their bodies and powers remain, independently of Kharost's false royal ancestry.

fifty-seven-minutes.note: Mallowbreak's launch crews, court, harbor registers and old relief works meet eighty-six years of agelessness and fifty-seven minutes of divine office. Orselle's commands displace water toward two neighboring coves; restoring ordinary flow requires prepared timber, evacuation and surrender of her gift. Her earlier shipwright liability remains.

head-priests-in-love.note: Levara and Ambel are in their seventh year of shared service at Brackwater. Mooring and departure rites already support working wharves under distinct gods. They complete the truce without converting each other; their private meeting six days later is planned, and the gods' silence does not end either jurisdiction.

saint-and-demon.note: Travel, an eight-month rural household and the Salt Crucible precede a catastrophe confined to a valley and the western basin edge while millions elsewhere survive. This is a proposed post-reawakening placement for a local magical loss; the final prose establishes no shared old root or universal extinction.

a-little-winter-for-sale.note: A desert settlement's stills, freight credit and wages depend on bounded, paid dragon cooling. The heat service and its maintenance contract connect this caravan economy to other specialist public works without identifying their makers.

the-night-harvest.note: A three-month ecological arrival becomes a dockside industry of hides, fuel, clinic material and debt. Six nights expose a local node's effects; the phenomenon's category and old-versus-new placement remain unresolved.

a-crown-for-the-endless-fire.note: Paid mine workers maintain vents and recently serviced stairs above older relief works. This is an operating extraction economy layered over inherited engineering, not proof that the surrounding civilization has collapsed.

the-name-the-water-took.note: An armed survey coerces Ioshka and charts an approach to people she wants to protect. Her seed stocks and route knowledge have practical value, but the expedition's funding and Braska's original motive are unstated. Destroying the map does not recover or absolve the captain's earlier choices.

stay-out-of-my-city.note: Nine years of Brackenport's exclusion challenge an already public hero economy whose battles close schools and consume civic life. Warren opposes its institutions while police, markets and council government continue. This public setting belongs beside the inhabited sky; its fate after the Bay is unknown.

the-attendance-ledger.note: Six months of anonymous assistance precede an exposure attack that the team successfully interrupts. No transformation is witnessed; classmates can explain the names and blurred footage as a stunt. The city's explicit disbelief motivates this proposed earlier reach, separate from later publicly taught and employed powers.

the-help-network.note: Beginning three afternoons after the showcase, private contacts spread help across countries and oceans over months. The international secrecy motivates historical distance from the later public sky. Attendance is its established predecessor; emergence into public life remains a proposed intervening history.

solstice-evening-bell.note: Solstice's coronation and circles lie centuries before the Battle of the Bay; by the battle she is already the last magical girl. The battle precedes the Glass Sea and begins the local aftermath sequence.

the-dress-they-brought-her.note: Damaged post-battle cameras, booking systems and labor procedures misidentify an ordinary prisoner. The supplied sequence places this after the Bay and before the museum; the prisoner is not Solstice.

the-count-was-131072.note: A living witness confronts a digital museum centuries after the Bay. This is the long public-memory aftermath of the same battle, not another immediate recovery scene.

the-future-that-refused-us.note: For three centuries, nine living readers have renewed Sablewake's binding prophecy every thirty years, enforcing a witnessed sequence at a cost to their memories. That guarantee has displaced reserves and backup crews. Its local, irreversible breach leaves rescues and accountability unfinished; it is distinct from a forecast that merely reports an act.

what-i-hate-most.note: Vantress sustains border wards through ceramic work, heat, pressure and municipal crews. It belongs beside engineered public power networks; no common source with the solar branches or an infernal realm is established.

daughter-of-the-sun.note: Four centuries of centralized solar dependence follow the Day of Glass. This established later history comes after Nell's home era and the Bay; decentralizing its branches does not restore or identify another magical system.

the-way-around.note: Paid relic hunters, expedition claims and multiple old scripts meet a dangerous surviving mechanism. Commercial exploration supplies its present-day context; the builders' civilization and the mechanism's category remain unknown.

the-morning-her-hand-moved.note: A community of 5,281 people has kept a thousand years of records on a body treated as permanent ground. Its movement forces evacuation but proves neither divine resurrection nor active magic.

all-accounts-due.note: Centuries of institutional history and thirty-one years of relic travel converge at the Array. Its release is the fixed terminal boundary of old material magic, not the consequence of one nearby city's decline.

four-million-falling.note: Orison’s civic founding story credits human builders after magic’s death. Generations maintain six reactors through incomplete inherited diagrams until fifty minutes force permanent grounding and evacuation. This is a positive remembered relation to extinction, with an unmeasured gap and a local technical fall.

the-five-minute-warranty.note: Coal, steam, quarry work and speaking-wire signals sustain a paid civic workshop. Replacement manufacture remains possible despite deferred maintenance. The rescue is completed and a permanent rebuild commissioned; the inquiry, rebuilding and financial consequences lie beyond the story.

the-ordinary-slime.note: Reservoir gauges, chemical assays and collective organism behavior meet a spillway bricked three generations earlier. This maintained agricultural watershed shares a material horizon with road societies; its ordinary biology is not a surviving magical root.

blade-calls-your-name.note: Hearthchain preserves a century of maintenance through skilled work and diagnostic tools. A temporary splice remains for six years because its replacement was falsely recorded as complete. Correcting attribution enables the immediate repair, while future maintenance and judgment remain separate obligations.

four-crowns-in-hiding.note: Two months after their central court falls, four sisters survive by respecting the independent knowledge and decisions of their sanctuary kingdoms. Their royal seal is genuine but its summons is false. This belongs with limits on crown authority; the relays serve that political relationship.

a-crown-in-the-bargain.note: Tareya makes marriage, territorial jurisdiction and emergency road aid separate choices. Independent titles, votes, engineers and debt terms make her bargain a close political neighbor to sanctuary compacts and competing courts; the optical register is a tool within that society.

the-weight-they-never-counted.note: Freight-adapted bodies persist in a manual road economy, but knowledge is unequal: the village moralizes strength while a caravan keeps an older anatomical survey and recognizes nutritional costs. An earlier culture of bodily revision is a useful proposed comparison; seedglass is not established as these people's ancestry.

coiled-together.note: Caravan work, road wardens and a local serpent queen depend on wages, warnings, translation and ordinary bodily capacities. Its proposed place beside inherited road societies is contextual; physiology does not prove the whole world is magicless.

the-last-monster.note: Searchers enter reused underground spaces occupied by varied living communities. The present is one of settlement and rescue within inherited architecture; neither the confinement's duration nor the builders' era is known.

the-walls-are-thick-enough.note: Tazri remains confined while an outside petition suspends the imperial levy for six months. Her marriage has not erased the duchy's treaty rights. This proposed older placement joins A Crown in the Bargain through competing personal and territorial obligations, while preserving the emperor's different law and coercion.

the-door-in-the-ivy.note: A queen retakes her capital seventeen years after a coup while ordinary trades and her caregiver’s fourteen-year marriage have continued. This local dynastic restoration overlaps other later inherited governments; it founds neither their states nor a new global age.

late-for-dinner.note: Wagons, crossbows, closed fields and burned bridges constrain an invaded territory and a three-thousand-person legion. Its ordinary material campaign belongs among the proposed older marcher economies without requiring magic in the incident.

save-that-dragon.note: Royal copper extraction, quarry works and a dismissed forge engineer bring the dragon into a territorial resource conflict. That context supports an old frontier placement even though the nature of its breath is unclassified.

golden-lion.note: Gaslit hereditary houses administer credit, votes and belonging through a male roll that has erased living survivors of a purge. Aldous's testimony recognizes the people behind a newly made replica cane while he remains on the Heron roll. Remembrance changes before the institution itself does.

the-courtesy-of-blades.note: Lacebridge's municipal yard connects teaching, patrol qualification and paid work upriver. Six months separate the recorded trial and rematch; Fiora has already accepted East Weir's head-instructor post before the farewell bout. This proposed educational horizon preserves an ordinary profession inside the older inhabited world.

only-eighteen.note: A long-lived childcare professional watches human twins grow from six weeks to eighteen amid wages, coaches, bakery apprenticeships and theater work. That ordinary care economy fits the older commercial road world; elf physiology establishes no global magic state.

the-rule-between-courses.note: Restaurants, cabinetmaking, rented rooms and smoking trams sustain a working town with furred, tail-bearing inhabitants and furniture made for their bodies. Friends update old assumptions about one another over dinner. This proposed older-town placement establishes neither a magical faculty nor an engineered origin for its population.

everyone-knows-her.note: An annual street festival runs through volunteer radios, timed closures, vendors and family work. The skater's apparent universal recognition comes from several ordinary sources, including prior visits and circulating descriptions. Reaching her niece also means dealing with the stall shift her sibling has covered.

before-she-gets-tired.note: A community arts center depends on volunteer labor, network payments, sound equipment and transport deadlines. Beatriz has already secured her first paid contract when she schedules a date around the Friday showcase and her first contract weekend. Work and courtship continue as separate commitments in this proposed modern horizon.

the-names-on-the-cups.note: Hinge's Seattle-named locality has Route 49, museum work and field-guide illustration. Across autumn to May, staff and customers replace inferred intimacy with direct knowledge and requested choices. The Long Dark placement is proposed; local names establish no literal Seattle history or connection to the Hinge matchmaking service in another story.

empire-within.note: An incumbent criminal leader counters forged orders and a rule that makes her own voice inadmissible to her crews. Phones, surviving witnesses, armed loyalties and compromised police determine what she can stop. The failed coup and canceled raid settle one night's confrontation while the rival's claims and the wider city remain.

the-other-twin.note: School, transport, insurance and specialist care must recognize two people sharing a body and circulation. Separate recordings let both state their wishes before a monitored temporary treatment; follow-up and ordinary coordination remain necessary. Neither an engineered origin nor a magical faculty is established.

the-station-between.note: Ruth's originating life includes ordinary modern kitchens, hospitals and phones. That material frame is proposed here; the afterlife platform's trains do not locate it within the material world's transport history.

the-ten-thousand-year-queen.note: Roughly ten thousand years after the last pharaoh’s entombment, reconstructed adults become participants in Merneith’s sixty-year infrastructure empire. This proposed later refounding shares an orbital interval with ordinary modernity; it supplies neither an exact gap from that modernity nor restored ancient minds.

terms-at-four.note: An armed orbital platform, detained workers, six hostages and a high court define one state's reach. Destroying the key and ejecting the lattice disarm that platform; retrieval would take months. Its proposed context is military authority and civilian recourse. The story does not establish the continental utility network or imperial jurisdiction shown in Merneith's history.

the-mercy-circuit.note: An aftermarket exchange supports prostheses, plasma tools, clinic seals and repair warranties. A courier's bounded repair belongs to a neighborhood economy built around personally modified bodies and paid technical craft.

sakura-hearted.note: Apartment electronics, recorded music and a home lathe coexist with a measured pulsed-field lift. Its small-scale consumer engineering closely fits A Little More Room, without requiring the same city or manufacturer.

a-little-more-room.note: An android's apartment, recordings, segmented joints and ordinary domestic negotiations share the consumer and workshop culture of Sakura-Hearted. Her cognitive filters have specified limits; they do not remove her will.

the-unfixed-face.note: Routine seedglass body plans support clinics, family businesses, trains and electric displays. A one-sunset archive deadline belongs to an established biomedical service economy, not its first discovery.

the-kill-she-wouldnt-take.note: Global broadcasts and an eighty-thousand-seat arena commercialize verified death-and-return technology. Forty-two previous returns make a stale status record an institutional hazard inside an ongoing public industry.

deja-vu-too-late.note: Paid tug crews, refinery cargo and an inhabited ring use a consented neural baseline with a ninety-six-second memory cost. Civilian orbital work is proposed alongside the ground and military technical societies; the warning is not a literal backward jump in time.

drone-down.note: Automated delivery, surveillance and working subsurface machinery persist beside bread queues and a closed station. This is an unequal functioning technical city, not proof that all its infrastructure has vanished.

the-driver-the-city-could-not-see.note: Automated transit and legally managed android identities dominate a city whose old river and freight roads remain inhabited. One night's escape reveals simultaneous technical centers and manual margins.

the-foundations-remember.note: Neural debt, commercial memory and rail work make recorded identity part of a city's property system. Evidence of older load-bearing masonry challenges founding propaganda; it does not identify the city with Eleven Foundations.

the-thirteenth-command.note: A guarded cistern faces starving neighboring settlements amid rifles, obsolete sensors and archived civic records. Edda's thirty-six years of dispatch knowledge make this a resource and maintenance history; temporary commands consume cells rather than will.

what-she-remembered-of-peace.note: At Anvek's request, independent technicians have severed the receiver that enabled involuntary command. Her civilian life precedes renewed war; she chooses to use bounded retained combat capacities alongside ordinary rescue equipment. This is not a restored remote override or a common liberation history with Loxan.

the-body-called-one.note: A Directorate pursues Loxan through the active systems of a supposedly decommissioned annex inside a ruined foundry. She recovers pilot addresses without their keys, escapes with a preserved body and requests medical help for both of them. The origin of her active mind and the other body's awareness remain unresolved; the rescue does not free every pilot.

last-watcher-of-jupiter.note: Thirteen thousand station residents depend on a staffed containment watch and its maintenance crews. Thirty years of service and an eight-year-old analog repair precede a forty-minute emergency. The pilots restore a working watch with no spare emitters; the deep signal's origin and the organism's intelligence remain unknown.

the-room-that-waited.note: Agrarian finders enter a buried, dormant launch facility whose controls they cannot identify. This is positive evidence of lost technical knowledge; its earlier use, builders’ fate, elapsed generations and cause of loss remain unknown.

leave-the-names.note: A caravan's salvage economy encounters a roofless city and a functioning mechanical metal-dissolution engine. Old civic nameplates survive into a later road culture, giving this ruin an actual material inheritance.

the-lights-beyond.note: Five centuries of enforced separation have hidden an inhabited orc city only two ridges away. Its ordinary transport, workshops and leisure defeat the scouts' inherited enemy image. This proposed later placement joins the ground-and-orbit stories through living contemporaries concealed by official history, rather than dating the human settlement by its apparent technology.

the-city-of-eleven-foundations.note: Eleven architectural and technical districts actively share one basin and one failing ring. Their simultaneous repair establishes a city of coexisting capacities, not eleven successive extinct civilizations.

rooms-before-sunrise.note: A six-hundred-lease living tower stands above reef foundations. Five temporarily detached housing bindings were wrongly archived, producing an urgent registration and repair crisis within a sophisticated municipal biology.

the-unfixed-song.note: A sailing city maintains hulls, gardens, forges and physical soundings while a new climate archive begins operating. Forecast access requires one authorized route song, including blame that current measurements cannot prove. This is an expansion of service with a historical cost, placed provisionally beside another maintained mobile city.

laughing-clouds.note: A municipal repair festival reuses failed batteries, tram infrastructure and solar cloth. Sensors and firmware remain ordinary working knowledge; reuse is not evidence that this city follows a global collapse.

kite-letters-below.note: An orbital society dates an alleged surface failure to 812 years earlier, then finds inhabited terraces and related service script below. Shared inheritance and diverged knowledge coexist in the same present; the official extinction claim is wrong.

apes-in-orbit.note: Surface cities of descendants of dinosaurs coexist with orbiting humans whose old maps miss them. Thermal transport and radio warnings solve one descent crisis; neither population is assigned a universal earlier or later evolutionary rung.

the-shadow-that-nested.note: An ancient sunshade shelters ordinary organisms above inhabited, technically capable surface grids. A tug crew's repair preserves both nests and some power; the structure's lost builders do not make the whole present a ruin.

the-star-that-followed-the-bells.note: A pastoral settlement's inherited bell practices help a wounded vessel coordinate with three independent satellites and reach a local orbit. Its sky contains working technology alongside local knowledge. The vessel's damaged route neither dates it after the stellar root burn nor identifies its travel with humanity's lattice.

the-first-people.note: An ordinary-looking home retains the root of humanity's vastly older interstellar roads. Burning it closes the fast network and leaves living civilizations dependent on slower travel, making this a genuine historical rupture within the story.

the-sky-remembers-us-return.note: Ordinary light carries the extinction's final image across ages of perfect material zero. The first bilateral link between Dalo and Keshen begins genuinely new magic; no old root is restored, and the earlier scenes do not share the link's date.

there-goes-your-name.note: A sheepfold, trained dog and household calling practice sustain a pastoral livelihood. Its active name working can belong on either side of the Long Dark; this later commons placement is proposed, not proof of the new system's first generation.

the-hollow-cask.note: Successive rebuilding, coerced living labor and neglect precede a twelve-week restoration and a smaller reopening. This actual local institutional refounding belongs with the proposed later civic craft societies, without assigning the decline to the Salt Crucible or another story’s catastrophe.

where-no-unicorn-stands.note: An orchard-and-channel kingdom and a mobile cloud city govern different parts of one water system. A four-day royal claim becomes a resource crisis between mature polities, not a founding rite for all new magic.

a-throne-neither-wanted.note: A monarchy maintains three centuries of forecast records beside medical study, hydrographic ships and beacon work. This proposed old placement follows its professional institutions and succession law; the forecast remains unrelated to Sablewake's guarantee.

the-kingdom-was-the-easy-part.note: Paid adventurers have already spent six years on a campaign when saving the kingdom becomes a retirement problem. The proposed old placement follows its expedition economy and labor history, not the presence of a crown in the title.

friends-of-the-night.note: Shalegate's siege depends on barley, pitch, beacons and six years of local knowledge about beast runs. This proposed old frontier placement joins material military contexts; its shadow ecology has no established connection to the Night Harvest.

a-darkness-written-under-skin.note: This society expects every newborn to carry a faculty-bearing mark and offers paid artificial grafts. Family dye work and the stigma of apparent absence shape a twenty-year case and six years of refusal. Its distinct hereditary expectations differ from both selective hero professions and eighteenth-year transformation; their lineage remains unestablished.

anatomy-of-a-god.note: A traveling practitioner with twelve years of regenerator care finds physical care apparatus inside an abandoned cult sanctuary. Professional bodily knowledge and inherited institutions locate this history; a claim of godhood does not prove one.

deaths-patron.note: Forty spellwrights, stored engines, municipal wards, sluices and a winchwright sustain an industrial magical city. A bounded death god participates in that labor system; the story belongs with public craft infrastructure rather than a generic rise of gods.

the-players-above.note: A material craft town maintains masonry, mills, irrigation and kilns above older silt. That working commons supplies its placed frame; the external players and their limited contact do not establish a separate age of this world.

what-the-town-owed-her.note: A modern town’s flood works and property services surround a witch whose rescue photograph is 114 years old. Open promises keep Evadne within the settlement; descendants inherit expectations rather than magical bonds. Her long life connects earlier communal aid to present-day choices.

the-inheritance-remembers.note: Modern road maintenance and GPS courier work disturb a threshold custom passed down after its meaning faded. Like Briar Hill, it needs fresh living replies when stored directions fail. Their close material and practical context motivates a shared pre-extinction horizon; a common town, maker or crossing system is not established.

the-last-bus-to-briar-hill.note: Modern courier and bus work meets a living crossing custom that requires a fresh freely given answer. This admitted magical history belongs before extinction. The Counted Road shares a proposed historical horizon through older routing practices amid modern services; the stories establish neither a common mechanism nor their mutual order.

the-cat-who-had-enough.note: Ten months after inheriting Mizzle, an owner faces a retail commitment left unanswered for nineteen days. The cat's compelled speech and dependence on ordinary care sit beside freelance work, a sister's separate business plans and losses that remain payable. The owner withdraws from the bakery without transferring that decision to Mizzle.

the-trouble-with-tuesdays.note: A family watch passes through dating, domestic life and many years of retained consequences in a modern service world. This admitted magical history precedes extinction; its rewinds do not identify any other crossing or time anomaly.

gods-afraid-of-grandma.note: At sixty-two, Valka enters a card game over old divine debts, interrupted when paramedics restart her heart. For forty-six years the gods divert bounded services to postpone her return and collection. At 108, the claim remains hers and the game resumes. Their domains, costs and ordinary medical limits do not establish a worldwide pantheon or immortality.

the-room-that-waited.end: A warning left by later agrarian finders

the-first-people.end: The root burn and slow-aid launches

lightning-carries-one.end: An ordinary journey eight years later
